threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think you can catch the Tube after 10pm without a struggle. Good luck with that during the strikes, mate.
Caught a night bus home from Brixton last week, saw a group of lads arguing over who had the best chicken shop. Classic South London.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I spotted the regulars at the 24/7 Späti arguing over the best Döner in the hood. The passion is real.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a kebab shop open at 3 AM that sells gourmet options like truffle sauce—classic Berlin meets high-end twist.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: A true local knows the secret of squeezing past the bus stop crowd at 16th and Mission without breaking stride—even when the BART's down.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 49 last week, packed with tourists trying to figure out how to pronounce 'Civic Center.' Classic San Francisco confusion.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they can just walk into any bar and get a great meal. Most locals know to check the daily menú del dia first.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by how they still scan the menu for a good ten minutes, lost on the local dishes, while the waiters look on with patience.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You keep asking for directions to the 'nearest tube' but you're in Dalston—it's all buses and overground. Tube? Good luck!
Caught a guy serenading the night bus with an old Elvis tune, while the driver just rolled his eyes. Only in Brixton, right?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I realized I was really home was when I heard a kid arguing with their parent in Turkish while a street musician played on a nearby corner. Perfect Neukölln vibe.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a currywurst stand next to a vintage vinyl shop, blasting techno while locals debate philosophy over street art.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a real local when they instinctively know to avoid 16th St BART around 5 PM. That’s not just traffic; it’s chaos.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy serenade the 19 bus passengers with a ukulele rendition of 'I Will Survive' while juggling three oranges. Classic Tenderloin.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think Gràcia is all about the plazas, but it’s the small bakeries tucked away on side streets that really serve the heart of the community.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by how they order 'café amb llet' instead of just coffee. Still trying to impress the barista, poor things.
